studies.label: Online experiment: printer-uses writing task with vs without ChatGPT

counts_source.quote: Forty-three people who failed the attention check were excluded from further analysis, leaving a final sample of 225.

arms.name: AI
arms.description: Randomly assigned participants were explicitly asked to make sure they used ChatGPT for the task; they reported their usage after the task (PDF p. 5, Section 2.2).

arms.name: Control
arms.description: Randomly assigned participants were forbidden from using ChatGPT for the task and reported any tools used afterwards (PDF p. 5, Section 2.2).

studies.task: Write approximately 100 words in 10 minutes describing as many unique uses as possible for a hypothetical printer that can print anything in 2097, while minimizing grammatical errors and maximizing clarity (PDF p. 5, Section 2.2).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (participant model and tier not stated)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 1, Section 1: ChatGPT release dated November 30, 2022; PDF p. 5, Section 2.2: participant instructions name ChatGPT. GPT4o and GPT4 Turbo are named as scoring models in Section 2.3, not identified as the participants' model.

preregistration.where: https://osf.io/dt5up?mode=&revisionId=&view_only= (PDF pp. 12-13, Pre-registration; also PDF p. 4, Section 2.1). The registration itself was not inspected.

estimates.outcome: Frequency (fluency): number of different printer uses in each participant's submission
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Total number of different uses proposed in the participant's submission. Automated counts using few-shot LLM prompts; the paper names GPT4o and GPT4 Turbo, without specifying which model's counts enter the analysis. The counts were validated against blinded human coding of a subset (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3). Coded category_count because the outcome is a count of ideas or categories.

estimates.notes: The treatment_mean and control_mean fields contain arm-level set counts, not participant averages; no averaging or difference calculation was performed. Numbers are transcribed from the prose on PDF p. 7 and assigned to the outcome using the bottom frequency panel of Fig. 5 on PDF p. 9, matching the reconciled screening form. The prose swaps the frequency/flexibility labels. Fig. 5's caption also reverses the use/nonuse wording; treatment assignment follows the figure's explicit AI/Control legend, checked visually. These numbers also appear in the prose and were not inferred from bar heights. Higher counts are interpreted by the paper as greater collective diversity (PDF p. 10, Section 4.2.3), although the calculation is underdescribed. No uncertainty, per-arm participant counts, or explicit count of participants contributing to this pooled outcome is printed. The paper does not numerically state n_units; the observation is each condition's full set of outputs. SI Table 5 was unavailable.

open_items: The supplement is referenced but absent from the supplied PDF. No local supplement was located. Requests through Python urllib to the article DOI and the named Oxford repository source both failed with a socket-permission error, so no supplementary information was used.

SI Table 3 is needed for the full-sample coefficients, SEs, p-values, model specification, and analysis counts for frequency, flexibility, inaccuracy, and unclarity. The main PDF supplies no full-sample numerical statistics for these outcomes (PDF pp. 5-6, Sections 3.1-3.2). Participant-level arm means and SDs are also unavailable.

AI and Control arm sizes, total randomized count, and outcome-specific participant counts are not printed. The overall study n_analyzed is transcribed as 225, while estimate-level counts remain null (PDF p. 4, Section 2.1).

The participant accounting is internally inconsistent: the paper states 266 completed, forty-three were excluded, and the final sample was 225. These printed counts do not reconcile; no replacement total has been calculated (PDF p. 4, Section 2.1). Perception analyses also use degrees of freedom without explicit analysis counts (PDF p. 8); no counts were inferred from them.
The timing of the attention check and whether randomization was stratified by native-language/prior-experience group are not specified (PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 2.1-2.2).

The group-level counting procedure, handling of duplicate ideas across participants, normalization by arm size, contributing participant counts, and uncertainty are not reported in the main PDF; SI Table 5 may clarify these matters (PDF p. 7, Section 3.2.3).

PDF p. 7 labels the full-pool values as Flexibility (635 vs. 552) and Frequency (442 vs. 313), whereas Fig. 5 on PDF p. 9 assigns them to frequency and flexibility respectively. This extraction follows the figure panel labels and explicit AI/Control legend, as does the reconciled screening form; the conflicting prose and caption wording are preserved in provenance notes.

The participants' ChatGPT model/tier, access route, and detailed usage instructions are not stated. The product release year is given on PDF p. 1, but it does not identify the model actually used. The researchers' scoring models are named on PDF p. 5, Section 2.3.
The paper names both GPT4o and GPT4 Turbo for counting uses/domains without saying which model's counts enter the outcome analyses (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3).

Preregistration is stated, but the available article does not designate a specific preregistered primary outcome; the registration was not inspected (PDF p. 4, Section 2.1; PDF pp. 12-13, Pre-registration).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10; extractor A. The entire supplied markdown was read from beginning to end, including Appendix A and references. All cited PDF pages were checked with pymupdf; the relevant Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 images were inspected in memory without creating files. Quote whitespace is normalized from PDF text. Empty source.fields arrays supply qualitative outcome/method provenance rather than numerical statistics. One randomized online study with individual assignment is eligible. The English-proficiency/prior-experience labels define pre-existing subgroups, not separate randomized studies or arms. Four full-sample individual-output records are retained with null statistics because the numerical pooled results are absent from the available source. Two diversity records retain printed set-level arm counts with no uncertainty. No standardized effects, differences, inferred sample sizes, or graph-derived point estimates were calculated. Inaccuracy and unclarity are kept as other output-scored companion outcomes on the divergent-use task; they are not creativity ratings and never enter pooling. The screening form reports no shared sample with another paper.
